bounded_finding_titles.M2-B45: restoration debt was process-wide and active ownership was object-local, so two ownership objects could own one process-wide flag independently
bounded_finding_titles.M2-B46: failed-start cleanup was complete when the child was reaped and the reference released, whatever the restoration reported
bounded_finding_titles.M2-B47: helper cleanup advertised a retry that no production caller could make progress on, because nothing invoked the process-wide settlement
bounded_finding_titles.M2-B48: the production call chain dropped every piece of incomplete cleanup evidence and every retry handle with the local wrapper that held it
bounded_finding_titles.M2-M49: the current reports claimed process-wide ownership, retryable failed-start cleanup, a settling helper retry and preparation-level propagation that the reproductions falsified

historical_delegated_qualifications.disposition: The first delegated qualification of this closure.  It failed two tests on one leaked per-effect cgroup and is preserved rather than discarded: it found a real gap -- the cleanup registry retained only process-ownership obligations and lost the effect-cgroup removal capability -- which the closure report records in full and this revision repairs.

The first delegated qualification of the subreaper/deadline closure.  Both failures were diagnosed and closed by that closure, and the failing transcript is preserved rather than discarded because a closure that hides its own failed qualification is the defect this milestone keeps closing.
The delegated run that qualified the subreaper/deadline closure.  It qualified the code as it stood two revisions ago and qualifies neither the previous closure nor this one.
The delegated run that qualified the ownership-debt/reap closure at the starting commit.  It is the prior_physical_qualification of this pass and does not qualify the code this pass changed.

known_limitations: The delegated physical qualification of this closure was performed by the operator against the modified worktree at the starting commit and passed: 507 tests, zero skips, zero failures, zero errors, under Delegate=yes, TasksMax=infinity and ADMISSIBLE_REQUIRE_DELEGATED_CGROUP=1.  It is a delegated-cgroup result on a development host: it is neither an installed-path qualification nor an independently accepted one, and neither is claimed.

The first delegated qualification of this closure ran 495 tests with zero skips and failed two on a leaked per-effect cgroup.  It is preserved as historical failed evidence, it qualifies nothing, and the gap it found -- a cleanup registry that retained only process-ownership obligations -- is repaired and re-qualified by the 507-test run above.

The 399-test delegated transcript of the previous closure is historical here.  It qualified the code as it stood at the starting commit and does not qualify the code this closure changed; a prior physical transcript never qualifies modified code.

The active child-subreaper ownership is now one record per process.  Two components that each expected a private ownership object share one depth, one baseline and one generation, which is the invariant; a component that relied on constructing its own independent owner would be relying on the defect this closes.

A SubreaperReference is valid only while the activation it was cut from is live, so a handle held across a contradiction, a discard, or a replacement reports invalid rather than stale-but-green.  Releasing it remains safe and remains exactly once.

The restoration-debt latch remains deliberately sticky and process-wide: until a settlement reads the owed baseline back, every acquisition in that process refuses.  Settlement is now attempted by helper close and by failed-start retry, so the ordinary path settles itself; a host on which PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER cannot be written at all still refuses every later effect in that process, which is the intended fail-closed behaviour.

The process cleanup registry has a finite capacity of 64 entries and refuses to start a further trusted helper when it is full.  Nothing sweeps it automatically; drain_incomplete_cleanups is called by the caller that has time to spend, exactly as retry_unsettled_failed_starts is.

A command that ran to completion inside a view whose cleanup did not finish is reported FAILED with error_code lifecycle_cleanup_incomplete.  The command's own facts and the export that already happened are preserved exactly; the tool outcome is classified so a green receipt cannot stand in front of an unresolved helper.

The acquisition gate remains fail-closed: a kernel that does not implement PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, or a policy that refuses it, refuses the whole effect.  This is the accepted M2-B37 behaviour and is not changed here.

While a trusted helper is alive this controller is a child subreaper.  An orphaned descendant of this controller that no effect owns would reparent here and is not reaped, because reaping it would require waitpid(-1) and could consume an unrelated child.  The window is bounded by helper lifetime and is disclosed rather than closed.

A DeprecationWarning about fork() in a multi-threaded process is emitted when the trusted mount-namespace helper is forked.  It is pre-existing, non-failing, not introduced by this closure, and is NOT closed here.
EVID-08 remains IMPLEMENTED: the retry counter belongs to the Milestone 3 cumulative budgets.
Independent acceptance and installed-path qualification are not claimed.
Milestone 3 remains forbidden and was not started.

delegated_run.detail: The operator ran the six qualification modules inside a transient Delegate=yes systemd unit under ADMISSIBLE_REQUIRE_DELEGATED_CGROUP=1, against the worktree carrying the B45, B46, B47, B48 and M49 changes at the starting commit.  Zero skips: under that variable a delegated test fails rather than skipping, so no result here can be a false green.  This run qualifies the revision that repairs the containment obligation the first run found missing; the first run's failing transcript is preserved as historical evidence and qualifies nothing.

supersedes_prior_current_report.no_second_snapshot_file: The M2-M36 model keeps exactly one current validation report.  The fourth-repair snapshot exists as a file because its bytes were otherwise unreachable; these bytes are reachable from git and from the immutable closure report, so no third file is created.
supersedes_prior_current_report.preserved_in: the git object at the starting commit, and -- in full -- in the immutable implementation/M2_OWNERSHIP_DEBT_REAP_CLOSURE_REPORT.json, which carries every claim the superseded report made about its own closure.
supersedes_prior_current_report.reason: The superseded report was the current artifact for the ownership-debt/reap closure.  It claimed that the process-wide restoration debt was closed while active ownership remained object-local, that failed-start cleanup was retryable, that helper cleanup was retryable while incomplete, and that _EffectPreparation.close propagated incomplete cleanup.  Each is falsified by an independent reproduction recorded in the closure report this one points at, and this pass changes the code its 399-test transcript qualified, so that transcript moves to prior_physical_qualification with qualifies_this_repair=false.

supersedes_validation_report.model: Option A -- versioned historical snapshot.  The superseded bytes are preserved under a clearly historical filename and the canonical filename carries the single current report, so a third party never has to decide which of two files is authoritative.
supersedes_validation_report.reason: M2-M36.  The superseded report carried the fourth-repair terminal refusal, a limitation declaring M2-B25 implemented but not physically qualified, cgroup delegation recorded as unavailable, and real delegated qualification recorded as false -- alongside two B25 closure objects recording a 125-test delegated run that had in fact succeeded.  One current artifact therefore asserted a physical qualification and its absence.  The bytes are preserved unchanged under the historical filename and this file is the sole current report.
